preamble: Voicing of the voiceless alveolar affricate [ts] to [dz]. In medieval Ibero-Romance it is part of the Western Romance lenition of intervocalic consonants: the [ts] from palatalized Latin c before front vowels was voiced between vowels, so Old Spanish and Old Galician-Portuguese have intervocalic z [dz] (dezir, vezino, fazer) against voiceless ç [ts] from geminates and post-consonantal positions. In Russian the same change is synchronic: /ts/ has the voiced allophone [dz] before a voiced obstruent.

examples.from: Vulgar Latin vēcīnus, intervocalic palatalized c > *[ts]
examples.note: The /dz/ later became [ð] and then [θ] (modern vecino).
The voiced affricate later deaffricated to modern Portuguese [z].
Regressive voicing assimilation: /ts/, /tɕ/ and /x/ have the voiced allophones [dz], [dʑ] and [ɣ] before voiced obstruents.

sources: Mackenzie, I. (n.d.). History of Spanish Consonants. Newcastle University. https://www.staff.ncl.ac.uk/i.e.mackenzie/consr.htm
Penny, R. (2002). A History of the Spanish Language (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511992827
